ch_model_communist_tt.en: #title $ch_model_communist$#!\nA $law_council_republic$ not under $law_anarchy$, or a $law_single_party_state$ with a $law_command_economy$ whose strongest interest group in government holds the $ideology_communist$ or $ideology_vanguardist$ ideology, even one with $law_national_supremacy$. $law_ethnostate$ makes it $ch_model_fascist$ instead.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_communist_tt.es: #title $ch_model_communist$#!\nUna $law_council_republic$ que no esté bajo $law_anarchy$, o un $law_single_party_state$ con $law_command_economy$ cuyo grupo de interés más fuerte en el gobierno tenga la ideología $ideology_communist$ o $ideology_vanguardist$, incluso con $law_national_supremacy$. Con $law_ethnostate$ pasa a ser $ch_model_fascist$ en su lugar.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_developmentalist_junta_tt.en: #title $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$#!\n$ch_model_junta_test_tt$ It also runs $law_interventionism$ or a $law_command_economy$ and keeps no law of the old order: no $law_serfdom$, $law_guild_system$, $law_peasant_levies$, $law_hereditary_bureaucrats$ or $law_feudal_contracts$; no $law_slave_trade$, $law_legacy_slavery$ or $law_debt_slavery$; and no $law_isolationism$, $law_traditionalism$, $law_extraction_economy$ or $law_industry_banned$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_developmentalist_junta_tt.es: #title $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$#!\n$ch_model_junta_test_tt$ Además aplica $law_interventionism$ o $law_command_economy$ y no conserva ninguna ley del viejo orden: ni $law_serfdom$, $law_guild_system$, $law_peasant_levies$, $law_hereditary_bureaucrats$ ni $law_feudal_contracts$; ni $law_slave_trade$, $law_legacy_slavery$ ni $law_debt_slavery$; ni $law_isolationism$, $law_traditionalism$, $law_extraction_economy$ ni $law_industry_banned$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_fascist_tt.en: #title $ch_model_fascist$#!\nA country with $law_ethnostate$; a $law_single_party_state$ with $law_national_supremacy$, unless its strongest interest group in government holds a left-wing ideology ($ideology_socialist$, $ideology_proletarian$, $ideology_social_democrat$, $ideology_communist$ or $ideology_vanguardist$); or a country with $law_national_supremacy$ under $law_autocracy$ whose strongest interest group in government holds the $ideology_fascist$ or $ideology_ethno_nationalist$ ideology.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_fascist_tt.es: #title $ch_model_fascist$#!\nUn país con $law_ethnostate$; un $law_single_party_state$ con $law_national_supremacy$, salvo que su grupo de interés más fuerte en el gobierno tenga una ideología de izquierdas ($ideology_socialist$, $ideology_proletarian$, $ideology_social_democrat$, $ideology_communist$ o $ideology_vanguardist$); o un país con $law_national_supremacy$ bajo $law_autocracy$ cuyo grupo de interés más fuerte en el gobierno tenga la ideología $ideology_fascist$ o $ideology_ethno_nationalist$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_hist_empty.en: No global model history yet. The next cultural recount records the first annual snapshot.
ch_model_hist_empty.es: Aún no hay historial global de modelos. El próximo recuento cultural registrará la primera instantánea anual.

ch_model_hist_note.en: #lore World cultural influence, 0–100%. One snapshot per year at the first recount; hover a bar for its date and all model shares. Old saves begin collecting after the update. Up to 100 annual snapshots are retained.#!
ch_model_hist_note.es: #lore Influencia cultural mundial, 0–100%. Una instantánea por año en el primer recuento; pasa el cursor sobre una barra para ver su fecha y la cuota de todos los modelos. Las partidas antiguas empiezan a recopilar datos tras la actualización. Se conservan hasta 100 instantáneas anuales.#!

ch_model_hist_title.es: Modelos políticos a lo largo del tiempo

ch_model_junta_test_tt.en: A military government: $law_autocracy$ or a $law_single_party_state$, with a $law_professional_army$ and $law_secret_police$ or a $law_militarized_police$.
ch_model_junta_test_tt.es: Un gobierno militar: $law_autocracy$ o un $law_single_party_state$, con un $law_professional_army$ y $law_secret_police$ o una $law_militarized_police$.

ch_model_liberal_tt.en: #title $ch_model_liberal$#!\nA country with $law_universal_suffrage$, or with $law_direct_democracy$ and $law_landed_voting$, $law_wealth_voting$ or $law_census_voting$, that also has $law_protected_speech$ or $law_right_of_assembly$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_liberal_tt.es: #title $ch_model_liberal$#!\nUn país con $law_universal_suffrage$, o con $law_direct_democracy$ y $law_landed_voting$, $law_wealth_voting$ o $law_census_voting$, que además tenga $law_protected_speech$ o $law_right_of_assembly$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_military_junta_tt.en: #title $ch_model_military_junta$#!\n$ch_model_junta_test_tt$ One that also runs $law_interventionism$ or a $law_command_economy$ and keeps no law of the old order counts as $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$ instead.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_military_junta_tt.es: #title $ch_model_military_junta$#!\n$ch_model_junta_test_tt$ Si además aplica $law_interventionism$ o $law_command_economy$ y no conserva ninguna ley del viejo orden, cuenta como $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$ en su lugar.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_order_tt.en: #lore A country that fits several models counts as the first of: $ch_model_anarchist$, $ch_model_communist$, $ch_model_fascist$, $ch_model_corporatist$, $ch_model_socialist$, $ch_model_technocratic$, $ch_model_royalist_absolutist$, $ch_model_royalist_constitutional$, $ch_model_religious$, $ch_model_reactionary$, $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$, $ch_model_military_junta$, $ch_model_liberal$, $ch_model_republican$, $ch_model_other$.#!
ch_model_order_tt.es: #lore Un país que encaja en varios modelos cuenta como el primero de estos: $ch_model_anarchist$, $ch_model_communist$, $ch_model_fascist$, $ch_model_corporatist$, $ch_model_socialist$, $ch_model_technocratic$, $ch_model_royalist_absolutist$, $ch_model_royalist_constitutional$, $ch_model_religious$, $ch_model_reactionary$, $ch_model_developmentalist_junta$, $ch_model_military_junta$, $ch_model_liberal$, $ch_model_republican$, $ch_model_other$.#!

ch_model_other_tt.en: #title $ch_model_other$#!\nA country that fits none of the other models.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_other_tt.es: #title $ch_model_other$#!\nUn país que no encaja en ninguno de los demás modelos.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_reactionary_tt.en: #title $ch_model_reactionary$#!\nA country with $law_autocracy$ and $law_state_religion$ that is not a $law_monarchy$, a $law_social_monarchy$ or a $law_theocracy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_reactionary_tt.es: #title $ch_model_reactionary$#!\nUn país con $law_autocracy$ y $law_state_religion$ que no sea una $law_monarchy$, una $law_social_monarchy$ ni una $law_theocracy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_republican_tt.en: #title $ch_model_republican$#!\nA $law_presidential_republic$ or $law_parliamentary_republic$, or a country under $law_direct_democracy$, that falls short of $ch_model_liberal$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_republican_tt.es: #title $ch_model_republican$#!\nUna $law_presidential_republic$ o $law_parliamentary_republic$, o un país bajo $law_direct_democracy$, que no llega a ser $ch_model_liberal$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_royalist_absolutist_tt.en: #title $ch_model_royalist_absolutist$#!\nA $law_monarchy$ or $law_social_monarchy$ with $law_autocracy$, even one with $law_national_supremacy$, unless it counts as $ch_model_fascist$: under $law_ethnostate$, or when its strongest interest group in government holds the $ideology_fascist$ or $ideology_ethno_nationalist$ ideology. $law_colonial_administration$ counts as $law_monarchy$, and $law_bakufu$ and $law_neo_absolutism$ count as $law_autocracy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_royalist_absolutist_tt.es: #title $ch_model_royalist_absolutist$#!\nUna $law_monarchy$ o $law_social_monarchy$ con $law_autocracy$, incluso con $law_national_supremacy$, salvo que cuente como $ch_model_fascist$: con $law_ethnostate$, o cuando su grupo de interés más fuerte en el gobierno tenga la ideología $ideology_fascist$ o $ideology_ethno_nationalist$. $law_colonial_administration$ cuenta como $law_monarchy$, y $law_bakufu$ y $law_neo_absolutism$ cuentan como $law_autocracy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_royalist_constitutional_tt.en: #title $ch_model_royalist_constitutional$#!\nA $law_monarchy$ or $law_social_monarchy$ without $law_autocracy$, even one with $law_universal_suffrage$. $law_colonial_administration$ counts as $law_monarchy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_royalist_constitutional_tt.es: #title $ch_model_royalist_constitutional$#!\nUna $law_monarchy$ o $law_social_monarchy$ sin $law_autocracy$, incluso con $law_universal_suffrage$. $law_colonial_administration$ cuenta como $law_monarchy$.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_model_socialist_tt.en: #title $ch_model_socialist$#!\nA country with $law_cooperative_ownership$, or with a $law_command_economy$ whose strongest interest group in government holds a left-wing ideology: $ideology_socialist$, $ideology_proletarian$, $ideology_social_democrat$, $ideology_communist$ or $ideology_vanguardist$. That holds even with $law_national_supremacy$; $law_ethnostate$ makes it $ch_model_fascist$ instead.\n$ch_model_order_tt$
ch_model_socialist_tt.es: #title $ch_model_socialist$#!\nUn país con $law_cooperative_ownership$, o con $law_command_economy$ cuyo grupo de interés más fuerte en el gobierno tenga una ideología de izquierdas: $ideology_socialist$, $ideology_proletarian$, $ideology_social_democrat$, $ideology_communist$ o $ideology_vanguardist$. Esto vale incluso con $law_national_supremacy$; con $law_ethnostate$ pasa a ser $ch_model_fascist$ en su lugar.\n$ch_model_order_tt$

ch_policy_funding_step_tt.en:
Each funding step adds:
[GetStaticModifier('ch_cultural_program_funding').GetDesc]
and costs, per step, @money!#R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('ch_program_funding_step_cost_display')|D]#!/week. At its current level the programme costs @money!#R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('ch_program_funding_total_cost_display')|D]#!/week.
#lore The cost scales with our GDP.#!
ch_policy_funding_step_tt.es:
Cada escalón de financiación añade:
[GetStaticModifier('ch_cultural_program_funding').GetDesc]
y cuesta, por escalón, @money!#R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('ch_program_funding_step_cost_display')|D]#!/semana. En su nivel actual, el programa cuesta @money!#R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('ch_program_funding_total_cost_display')|D]#!/semana.

ch_tier_blurb_hegemon.en: We are the undisputed centre of global culture. Our art, language and political model are the world's aspiration.

ch_tier_blurb_minor.en: Our cultural output is modest. Few outside our borders look to us for inspiration.

ch_tier_blurb_moderate.en: We have a growing cultural footprint, but we are far from dominant.

ch_tier_blurb_negligible.en: We have virtually no global cultural presence.

ch_tier_blurb_significant.en: Our culture resonates beyond our borders. The world is taking notice of our achievements.
ch_tier_blurb_significant.es: Nuestra cultura resuena más allá de nuestras fronteras. El mundo empieza a fijarse en nuestros logros.

covert_backlash_no_lobby_tt.es: Ningún [concept_political_lobby|l] del país favorece a [SCOPE.sCountry('detected_by_country').GetName], así que ninguno pierde [concept_political_lobby_appeasement|l]

covert_cis_one_protector_tt.es: Ningún otro país apoya ya la contrainteligencia del objetivo

covert_cis_target_is_friend_tt.en: The target is a friend: cordial relations together with an alliance, a defensive pact, a shared power bloc or a subject tie, or amicable relations alone
covert_cis_target_is_friend_tt.es: El objetivo es un amigo: relaciones cordiales junto con una alianza, un pacto de defensa, un bloque de poder compartido o un vínculo de subordinación, o bien solo relaciones amables

covert_counterintel_support_phase_tt.en: For its first six months the support is #R Preparatory#! and does nothing. From month 6 it is #Y Establishing#! and adds the defences listed; from month 12 it is #G Fully Operational#! and they are #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_phase_full_mult')|0]#!. Raising its priority multiplies them again, #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_2_effect_mult')|2]#! at priority 2 and #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_3_effect_mult')|2]#! at priority 3, for a larger share of the covert budget.
covert_counterintel_support_phase_tt.es: Durante sus seis primeros meses el apoyo es #R Preparatorio#! y no hace nada. Desde el mes 6 está #Y En implantación#! y añade las defensas indicadas; desde el mes 12 es #G Plenamente operativo#! y estas se multiplican: #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_phase_full_mult')|0]#!. Aumentar su prioridad las multiplica de nuevo: #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_2_effect_mult')|2]#! con prioridad 2 y #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_3_effect_mult')|2]#! con prioridad 3, a cambio de una parte mayor del presupuesto encubierto.

covert_counterintel_support_public_tt.en: An open arrangement, not a secret: it is never rolled for detection and never exposed. It gives us nothing inside [SCOPE.sCountry('target_country').GetName]: no network there and no Tradecraft.
covert_counterintel_support_public_tt.es: Un acuerdo abierto, no secreto: nunca se comprueba su detección y nunca queda expuesto. No nos da nada dentro de [SCOPE.sCountry('target_country').GetName]: ni una red allí ni Técnicas de espionaje.

covert_cultivate_assets_extra_tt.en: No effect on the target: grows our network there faster than any other operation.
covert_cultivate_assets_extra_tt.es: Sin efecto en el objetivo: hace crecer nuestra red allí más rápido que cualquier otra operación.

covert_exposure_third_party_tt.en: Every country in the target's [concept_power_bloc] and every one of their treaty allies loses #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_exposure_third_party_relations_display')|0]#! [concept_relations] with us
covert_exposure_third_party_tt.es: Todo país del [concept_power_bloc|l] del objetivo y todos sus aliados por tratado pierden #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_exposure_third_party_relations_display')|0]#! de [concept_relations|l] con nosotros

covert_friend_target_warning_tt.en: [SCOPE.sCountry('target_country').GetName] is a friend. If this operation is exposed, the lobby at home that favours them will be angered and the government will lose [concept_legitimacy].
covert_friend_target_warning_tt.es: [SCOPE.sCountry('target_country').GetName] es un amigo. Si esta operación queda al descubierto, el lobby nacional que lo favorece se enfurecerá y el gobierno perderá [concept_legitimacy|l].

covert_ideological_subversion_extra_tt.en: The [Concept('concept_political_movement', 'political movements')] in the target that align with our governing ideology get #R +5%#! [concept_activism] and #R +10%#! [concept_pop] attraction. This part does not grow once the operation is fully operational.
covert_ideological_subversion_extra_tt.es: Los [Concept('concept_political_movement', 'movimientos políticos')] del objetivo afines a nuestra ideología de gobierno obtienen #R +5%#! de [concept_activism|l] y #R +10%#! de atracción de [Concept('concept_pop', 'colectivos')]. Esta parte no aumenta una vez que la operación está plenamente operativa.

covert_infrastructure_sabotage_extra_tt.en: Each month we also strike one of the target's states with buildings, chosen at random: for three months it has #R -15%#! [concept_infrastructure] and #R -10%#! building [concept_throughput].
covert_infrastructure_sabotage_extra_tt.es: Cada mes golpeamos además un estado del objetivo con edificios, elegido al azar: durante tres meses sufre #R -15%#! de [concept_infrastructure|l] y #R -10%#! de [concept_throughput|l] de los edificios.

covert_known_expose_effect_tt.en: We make the operation public. Its sponsor answers for it before the world, in infamy and in its relations with us; its network inside our country loses #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_net_burn_loss')|0]#! strength; interest groups here that favour it lose standing; and our network inside its service stops growing from this operation. The operation ends.
covert_known_expose_effect_tt.es: Hacemos pública la operación. Su patrocinador responde de ella ante el mundo, en infamia y en sus relaciones con nosotros; su red dentro de nuestro país pierde #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_net_burn_loss')|0]#! de fuerza; los grupos de interés de aquí que lo favorecen pierden influencia; y nuestra red dentro de su servicio deja de crecer por esta operación. La operación termina.

covert_op_burned_tt.en: The compromised operation will be terminated, our network in their country loses #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_net_burn_loss')|0]#! strength, and our agency's Tradecraft falls by #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tradecraft_burn_loss_value')|0]#!.
covert_op_burned_tt.es: La operación comprometida se dará por terminada, nuestra red en su país pierde #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_net_burn_loss')|0]#! de fuerza y las Técnicas de espionaje de nuestra agencia bajan #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tradecraft_burn_loss_value')|0]#!.

covert_op_capacity_comms_tt.es: No hay cupos de interrupción de las comunicaciones disponibles — reduce las operaciones de comunicaciones activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_industrial_tt.es: No hay cupos de espionaje industrial disponibles — reduce las operaciones de espionaje activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_influence_tt.en: No influence campaign slots available — reduce active influence operations or increase covert capacity.
covert_op_capacity_influence_tt.es: No hay cupos de campaña de influencia disponibles — reduce las operaciones de influencia activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_infrastructure_tt.en: No [concept_infrastructure] sabotage slots available — reduce active sabotage operations or increase covert capacity.
covert_op_capacity_infrastructure_tt.es: No hay cupos de sabotaje de [concept_infrastructure|l] disponibles — reduce las operaciones de sabotaje activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_military_tt.en: No military espionage slots available — reduce active military espionage operations or increase covert capacity.
covert_op_capacity_military_tt.es: No hay cupos de espionaje militar disponibles — reduce las operaciones de espionaje militar activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_regime_change_tt.es: No hay cupos de cambio de régimen disponibles — reduce las operaciones de cambio de régimen activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_capacity_secure_material_tt.en: No loose-material search slots available — reduce active searches or increase covert capacity.

covert_op_capacity_space_espionage_tt.es: No hay cupos de espionaje espacial disponibles — reduce las operaciones de espionaje espacial activas o aumenta la capacidad encubierta.

covert_op_detection_warning_tt.en: @warning! Detection Risk: Each month your agents are active, there is a chance they are discovered. If the target then exposes the operation, it causes [concept_infamy] and diplomatic consequences.
covert_op_detection_warning_tt.es: @warning! Riesgo de detección: cada mes que tus agentes están activos, existe la posibilidad de que los descubran. Si el objetivo expone entonces la operación, provoca [concept_infamy|l] y consecuencias diplomáticas.

covert_op_phase_warning_tt.en: For its first six months the operation is #R Preparatory#! and does nothing. From month 6 it is #Y Establishing#! and has the effects listed; from month 12 it is #G Fully Operational#! and they are #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_phase_full_mult')|0]#!. A network of ours already in the target shortens the wait. Raising the operation's priority multiplies them again, #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_2_effect_mult')|2]#! at priority 2 and #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_3_effect_mult')|2]#! at priority 3, for a larger share of the covert budget. A later phase also costs more when an operation is exposed: the further along the network, the heavier the infamy and the breach in relations.
covert_op_phase_warning_tt.es: Durante sus seis primeros meses la operación es #R Preparatoria#! y no hace nada. Desde el mes 6 está #Y En implantación#! y produce los efectos indicados; desde el mes 12 es #G Plenamente operativa#! y estos se multiplican: #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_phase_full_mult')|0]#!. Una red nuestra ya presente en el objetivo acorta la espera. Aumentar la prioridad de la operación los multiplica de nuevo: #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_2_effect_mult')|2]#! con prioridad 2 y #G x[GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_op_priority_3_effect_mult')|2]#! con prioridad 3, a cambio de una parte mayor del presupuesto encubierto. Además, una fase posterior cuesta más cuando se expone una operación: cuanto más avanzada está la red, mayores son la infamia y la ruptura de relaciones.

covert_op_preview_header_tt.en: The operation's effects are listed at #bold base strength#!, as they are once it is established and at priority 1.
covert_op_preview_header_tt.es: Los efectos de la operación se muestran con #bold intensidad base#!, la que tienen una vez implantada y con prioridad 1.

covert_op_self_effect_note_espionage_tt.en: Stolen [concept_technology] adds up: each operation steals from its own target. An operation ends on its own once its target has nothing left we could take.
covert_op_self_effect_note_espionage_tt.es: La [concept_technology|l] robada se acumula: cada operación roba a su propio objetivo. Una operación termina por sí sola cuando su objetivo ya no tiene nada que podamos llevarnos.

covert_op_self_effect_note_tt.en: Our own gains come from our strongest operation of this type and do not add up: a second one, against another country, gives us nothing more.
covert_op_self_effect_note_tt.es: Nuestras propias ganancias proceden de nuestra operación más potente de este tipo y no se acumulan: una segunda, contra otro país, no nos da nada más.

covert_op_tech_theft_preview_military_tt.en: Each month, progress toward a military [concept_technology] the target has researched and we have not: our current research if it is one, otherwise a random one we could research now. At base strength it is #G [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tech_theft_share_percent_display')|0]%#! of the technology's era cost.
covert_op_tech_theft_preview_military_tt.es: Cada mes, avance hacia una [concept_technology|l] militar que el objetivo ha investigado y nosotros no: nuestra investigación actual si lo es, y si no, una al azar que podamos investigar ahora. Con intensidad base equivale al #G [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tech_theft_share_percent_display')|0]%#! del coste de era de la tecnología.

covert_op_tech_theft_preview_production_.en: Each month, progress toward a production [concept_technology] the target has researched and we have not: our current research if it is one, otherwise a random one we could research now. At base strength it is #G [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tech_theft_share_percent_display')|0]%#! of the technology's era cost.
covert_op_tech_theft_preview_production_.es: Cada mes, avance hacia una [concept_technology|l] de producción que el objetivo ha investigado y nosotros no: nuestra investigación actual si lo es, y si no, una al azar que podamos investigar ahora. Con intensidad base equivale al #G [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_tech_theft_share_percent_display')|0]%#! del coste de era de la tecnología.

covert_regime_change_extra_tt.en: Once the operation is fully operational, any [concept_coup] already under way in the target gains #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_regime_change_coup_push')|0]#! progress every month, whatever the priority.
covert_regime_change_extra_tt.es: Cuando la operación está plenamente operativa, todo [concept_coup|l] que ya esté en marcha en el objetivo gana #R [GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('covert_regime_change_coup_push')|0]#! de avance cada mes, sea cual sea la prioridad.

gm_arch_row_dig_permit.es: En el extranjero, mediante un permiso de excavación de [ScriptContainer.MakeScope.Var('gm_site_view_state').GetState.GetOwner.GetName]: los hallazgos se quedan allí y obtenemos Erudición extranjera

gm_arch_row_open_detail.es: Abierto a la excavación: aporta #v [ScriptContainer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('gm_arch_disp_levels')|0]#! niveles y #v [ScriptContainer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('gm_arch_disp_grandeur')|0]#! de [concept_grandeur|l]

gm_arch_scholarship_desc.en: Our expedition dug abroad and left the finds with the host. The site reports, the lectures and the name on the excavation are ours.
gm_arch_scholarship_desc.es: Nuestra expedición excavó en el extranjero y dejó los hallazgos al país anfitrión. Los informes del yacimiento, las conferencias y el nombre de la excavación son nuestros.

gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_dug.en: Divers working in turns over $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place$, south of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_antikythera_mechanism').GetName], have brought up bronze and marble statues, glassware and amphorae from a ship that sank in the first century BC. Among the corroded lumps lifted from the wreck is a box of bronze gearwheels, at least thirty of them, finely toothed and inscribed: an instrument for reckoning the motions of the Sun, the Moon and the planets.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_history$
gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_dug.es: Unos buzos que trabajan por turnos sobre $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place$, al sur de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_antikythera_mechanism').GetName], han sacado estatuas de bronce y de mármol, cristalería y ánforas de un barco que se hundió en el siglo I a. C. Entre los fragmentos corroídos extraídos del pecio hay una caja de engranajes de bronce, al menos treinta, de dientes finos e inscritos: un instrumento para calcular los movimientos del Sol, la Luna y los planetas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_history$

gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_found.en: Sponge divers sheltering from a storm, south of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_antikythera_mechanism').GetName], have dived on $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place$ and come up with a bronze arm. They report statues on the seabed, half buried in sand, deeper than any diver works for long.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_history$
gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_found.es: Unos buceadores de esponjas que se refugiaban de una tormenta, al sur de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_antikythera_mechanism').GetName], se han sumergido en $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place$ y han salido con un brazo de bronce. Informan de estatuas en el lecho marino, medio enterradas en la arena, a más profundidad de la que ningún buzo soporta trabajar mucho tiempo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_history$

gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_histo.en: Greek sponge divers found the wreck in 1900, and the salvage of 1900-1901 for the Greek government was the first great underwater excavation: one diver died and two were paralysed. The mechanism, noticed in 1902, was understood only through Derek de Solla Price's work and X-ray and CT scans in the late twentieth century; it predicted eclipses and the four-year cycle of the Games. It is in the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.
gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_histo.es: Unos buceadores de esponjas griegos encontraron el pecio en 1900, y el rescate de 1900-1901 para el gobierno griego fue la primera gran excavación submarina: un buzo murió y dos quedaron paralizados. El mecanismo, advertido en 1902, solo se comprendió gracias al trabajo de Derek de Solla Price y a las radiografías y tomografías de finales del siglo XX; predecía eclipses y el ciclo cuatrienal de los Juegos. Se conserva en el Museo Arqueológico Nacional de Atenas.

gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place.en: a Roman-era wreck at the foot of a cliff off the island of Antikythera
gm_arch_site_antikythera_mechanism_place.es: un naufragio de época romana al pie de un acantilado frente a la isla de Anticitera

gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_dug.en: In a house and workshop in $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_bust_of_nefertiti').GetName], the excavators have found a sculptor's studio, its owner named Thutmose on an ivory horse blinker, with plaster casts and unfinished heads of the royal family. Among them lay a bust of painted limestone of Queen Nefertiti, with the tall blue crown and the long neck, its colours almost untouched and one eye never inlaid.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history$
gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_dug.es: En una casa y taller situados en $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_bust_of_nefertiti').GetName], los excavadores han hallado el estudio de un escultor, con el nombre de su dueño, Tutmosis, en una anteojera de caballo de marfil, con moldes de yeso y cabezas inacabadas de la familia real. Entre ellos yacía un busto de piedra caliza pintada de la reina Nefertiti, con la alta corona azul y el cuello largo, con sus colores casi intactos y un ojo sin incrustar nunca.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history$

gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_found.en: Akhenaten built a new capital in the desert, and the pharaohs who followed abandoned it; its boundary stelae still stand in the cliffs. Our scholars believe $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_bust_of_nefertiti').GetName], have hardly been disturbed since, and that its houses and workshops lie as their owners left them.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history$
gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_found.es: Akenatón construyó una nueva capital en el desierto, y los faraones que le siguieron la abandonaron; sus estelas fronterizas aún se alzan en los acantilados. Nuestros eruditos creen que en $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_bust_of_nefertiti').GetName], apenas se ha tocado nada desde entonces, y que sus casas y talleres yacen tal como los dejaron sus dueños.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history$

gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history.en: Ludwig Borchardt's German expedition found the bust on 6 December 1912. In the division of finds of January 1913 with Gustave Lefebvre of the Antiquities Service it went to the German side, and it has been in Berlin ever since, now in the Neues Museum. Egypt has asked for its return since the 1920s.
gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_history.es: La expedición alemana de Ludwig Borchardt encontró el busto el 6 de diciembre de 1912. En el reparto de hallazgos de enero de 1913 con Gustave Lefebvre, del Servicio de Antigüedades, pasó a la parte alemana, y desde entonces está en Berlín, hoy en el Neues Museum. Egipto pide su devolución desde la década de 1920.

gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place.en: the ruins of Akhetaten at Amarna, on the east bank of the Nile
gm_arch_site_bust_of_nefertiti_place.es: las ruinas de Ajetatón en Amarna, en la orilla oriental del Nilo

gm_arch_site_caral_supe_dug.en: On $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_caral_supe').GetName], the excavators have uncovered a planned city of six platform pyramids, sunken circular plazas, houses and workshops, with no pottery, no weapons and no walls. Its builders traded cotton for fish with the coast and played flutes of pelican and condor bone; the reed bags of stones in the pyramids' fill, dated by radiocarbon, put the city at about 2600 BC.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history$
gm_arch_site_caral_supe_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_caral_supe').GetName], los excavadores han sacado a la luz una ciudad planificada de seis pirámides de plataforma, plazas circulares hundidas, casas y talleres, sin cerámica, sin armas y sin murallas. Sus constructores intercambiaban algodón por pescado con la costa y tocaban flautas de hueso de pelícano y de cóndor; las bolsas de juncos con piedras del relleno de las pirámides, datadas por radiocarbono, sitúan la ciudad hacia 2600 a. C.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history$

gm_arch_site_caral_supe_found.en: The low mounds on $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_caral_supe').GetName], have long been taken for hills, or for the ruins of some late and minor town. Our archaeologists have noticed that they are built, that they are pyramids, and that the pottery that dates every other Andean site is missing.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history$
gm_arch_site_caral_supe_found.es: Los montículos bajos que hay en $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_caral_supe').GetName], se han tomado durante mucho tiempo por colinas, o por las ruinas de algún pueblo tardío y menor. Nuestros arqueólogos han advertido que están construidos, que son pirámides, y que falta la cerámica que data todos los demás yacimientos andinos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history$

gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history.en: Paul Kosok noted the site in 1948, but only when Ruth Shady Solís began digging in 1994 was it understood; radiocarbon dates published in 2001 made Caral the oldest city then known in the Americas, as old as the pyramids of Giza. It became a World Heritage Site in 2009.
gm_arch_site_caral_supe_history.es: Paul Kosok señaló el yacimiento en 1948, pero solo se comprendió cuando Ruth Shady Solís empezó a excavar en 1994; las dataciones por radiocarbono publicadas en 2001 hicieron de Caral la ciudad más antigua conocida entonces en América, tan antigua como las pirámides de Guiza. Fue declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 2009.

gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place.en: the desert terraces above the Supe valley at Caral
gm_arch_site_caral_supe_place.es: las terrazas desérticas sobre el valle del Supe, en Caral

gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_dug.en: In eleven of $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_dead_sea_scrolls').GetName], and in the ruins of the settlement below, the searchers have recovered the remains of about nine hundred manuscripts, most in fragments, from the third century BC to the first century AD: every book of the Hebrew Bible except Esther, a complete scroll of Isaiah, and the rules, hymns and calendars of a sect awaiting the end of days.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history$
gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_dug.es: En once de $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_dead_sea_scrolls').GetName], y en las ruinas del asentamiento situado debajo, los investigadores han recuperado los restos de unos novecientos manuscritos, la mayoría en fragmentos, del siglo III a. C. al siglo I d. C.: todos los libros de la Biblia hebrea salvo Ester, un rollo completo de Isaías, y las reglas, himnos y calendarios de una secta que aguardaba el fin de los días.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history$

gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_found.en: A Bedouin shepherd looking for a stray goat in $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_dead_sea_scrolls').GetName], threw a stone into a cave and heard pottery break. Inside were tall jars holding rolls of leather, wrapped in linen and written in Hebrew, which a dealer in Bethlehem has bought for a few pounds.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history$
gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_found.es: Un pastor beduino que buscaba una cabra extraviada en $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_dead_sea_scrolls').GetName], lanzó una piedra a una cueva y oyó romperse cerámica. Dentro había altas jarras con rollos de cuero, envueltos en lino y escritos en hebreo, que un comerciante de Belén ha comprado por unas pocas libras.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history$

gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history.en: Muhammad edh-Dhib found the first cave in 1946 or 1947. Bedouin and archaeologists, Roland de Vaux among them, searched the other caves until 1956. The great Isaiah scroll is about a thousand years older than any manuscript of the Hebrew Bible known before. The large scrolls are in the Shrine of the Book in Jerusalem, and the Copper Scroll is in Amman.
gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_history.es: Muhammad edh-Dhib encontró la primera cueva en 1946 o 1947. Beduinos y arqueólogos, entre ellos Roland de Vaux, registraron las demás cuevas hasta 1956. El gran rollo de Isaías es unos mil años más antiguo que cualquier manuscrito de la Biblia hebrea conocido hasta entonces. Los rollos grandes están en el Santuario del Libro, en Jerusalén, y el Rollo de Cobre, en Amán.

gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place.en: the caves in the cliffs above Khirbet Qumran, on the northwest shore of the Dead Sea
gm_arch_site_dead_sea_scrolls_place.es: las cuevas de los acantilados sobre Khirbet Qumrán, en la orilla noroeste del mar Muerto

gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_dug.en: From $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_deir_el_bahari_cache').GetName], a corridor opens into chambers crowded with coffins: some fifty royal and noble mummies, Seqenenre Tao, Ahmose, Thutmose III, Seti I and Ramesses II among them, hidden there by priests of the Twenty-first Dynasty to save them from tomb robbers, with their coffins, canopic jars and funerary goods.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_history$
gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_dug.es: Desde $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_deir_el_bahari_cache').GetName], un corredor se abre a cámaras repletas de ataúdes: unas cincuenta momias reales y nobles, entre ellas Seqenenre Tao, Ahmose, Tutmosis III, Seti I y Ramsés II, ocultadas allí por sacerdotes de la dinastía XXI para salvarlas de los saqueadores de tumbas, con sus ataúdes, vasos canopos y ajuares funerarios.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_history$

gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_found.en: Royal scarabs, papyri and funerary figures of pharaohs have been turning up in the antiquities shops of Luxor, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_deir_el_bahari_cache').GetName], for years. Our inspectors have traced them to a family of the village of Gurna, who have at last led them to $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place$.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_history$
gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_found.es: Desde hace años aparecen escarabeos reales, papiros y figuras funerarias de faraones en las tiendas de antigüedades de Luxor, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_deir_el_bahari_cache').GetName]. Nuestros inspectores han seguido su rastro hasta una familia del pueblo de Gurna, que por fin los ha llevado hasta $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place$.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_history$

gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_histor.en: The Abd el-Rassul brothers found the tomb, now called DB320, around 1871 and sold its contents for a decade. In 1881, after one brother confessed, Émile Brugsch of the Antiquities Service emptied it in a few days, and as the mummies went downriver to Cairo, villagers along the banks mourned them. They are in the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization.
gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_histor.es: Los hermanos Abd el-Rassul encontraron la tumba, hoy llamada DB320, hacia 1871 y vendieron su contenido durante una década. En 1881, después de que un hermano confesara, Émile Brugsch, del Servicio de Antigüedades, la vació en pocos días, y mientras las momias bajaban por el río hacia El Cairo, los aldeanos de las orillas las lloraron. Se encuentran en el Museo Nacional de la Civilización Egipcia.

gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place.en: a shaft in the cliffs south of Hatshepsut's temple at Deir el-Bahari, on the west bank at Thebes
gm_arch_site_deir_el_bahari_cache_place.es: un pozo en los acantilados al sur del templo de Hatshepsut en Deir el-Bahari, en la orilla occidental de Tebas

gm_arch_site_delphi_dug.en: With the houses of $gm_arch_site_delphi_place$ moved to a new site, the excavators have uncovered, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_delphi').GetName], the sanctuary of Apollo: the Sacred Way climbing past the treasuries of the cities, the Temple of Apollo where the Pythia prophesied, the theatre and the stadium above it, and a life-sized bronze charioteer cast about 475 BC, with eyes of glass and stone and eyelashes of copper.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_delphi_history$
gm_arch_site_delphi_dug.es: Una vez trasladadas a un nuevo emplazamiento las casas que había en $gm_arch_site_delphi_place$, los excavadores han sacado a la luz, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_delphi').GetName], el santuario de Apolo: la Vía Sacra que sube entre los tesoros de las ciudades, el templo de Apolo donde profetizaba la Pitia, el teatro y, por encima, el estadio, y un auriga de bronce de tamaño natural fundido hacia 475 a. C., con ojos de vidrio y piedra y pestañas de cobre.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_delphi_history$

gm_arch_site_delphi_found.en: The houses of $gm_arch_site_delphi_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_delphi').GetName], stand on the sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi: they are built of the oracle's stones, and inscriptions turn up in their walls. Our scholars want the village moved, so that the sanctuary beneath it can be dug.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_delphi_history$
gm_arch_site_delphi_found.es: Las casas que hay en $gm_arch_site_delphi_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_delphi').GetName], se alzan sobre el santuario de Apolo en Delfos: están construidas con las piedras del oráculo, y en sus muros aparecen inscripciones. Nuestros eruditos quieren que se traslade el pueblo, para poder excavar el santuario que hay debajo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_delphi_history$

gm_arch_site_delphi_history.en: The French School at Athens won the right to dig Delphi in 1891, paying to move the villagers, and its Great Excavation ran from 1892 to 1903 under Théophile Homolle; the Charioteer was found in 1896. The finds stayed in Greece, in the museum at Delphi.
gm_arch_site_delphi_history.es: La Escuela Francesa de Atenas obtuvo el derecho a excavar Delfos en 1891, pagando el traslado de los aldeanos, y su Gran Excavación se desarrolló de 1892 a 1903 bajo Théophile Homolle; el Auriga apareció en 1896. Los hallazgos se quedaron en Grecia, en el museo de Delfos.

gm_arch_site_delphi_place.en: the village of Kastri, on the slopes of Mount Parnassus
gm_arch_site_delphi_place.es: el pueblo de Kastri, en las laderas del monte Parnaso

gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_dug.en: On $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_gobekli_tepe').GetName], the excavators have uncovered rings of T-shaped limestone pillars up to five metres tall, carved with foxes, boars, snakes, vultures and scorpions, some with arms and hands as if they were figures. They were raised about 9500 BC by hunters and gatherers, before farming, pottery or the wheel, and later filled in.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history$
gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_gobekli_tepe').GetName], los excavadores han sacado a la luz anillos de pilares de piedra caliza en forma de T, de hasta cinco metros de altura, tallados con zorros, jabalíes, serpientes, buitres y escorpiones, algunos con brazos y manos como si fueran figuras. Fueron levantados hacia 9500 a. C. por cazadores y recolectores, antes de la agricultura, la cerámica o la rueda, y más tarde fueron rellenados.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history$

gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_found.en: A survey in the 1960s recorded $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_gobekli_tepe').GetName], as a medieval cemetery on a natural hill strewn with broken limestone slabs. Our archaeologists have looked again: the slabs are the tops of carved pillars, and the flint scattered across the hill is far older than any cemetery.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history$
gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_found.es: Un estudio de la década de 1960 registró $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_gobekli_tepe').GetName], como un cementerio medieval en una colina natural sembrada de lajas de piedra caliza rotas. Nuestros arqueólogos han vuelto a mirar: las lajas son las cimas de pilares tallados, y el sílex esparcido por la colina es mucho más antiguo que cualquier cementerio.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history$

gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history.en: Klaus Schmidt of the German Archaeological Institute recognised the site in 1994 and dug it from 1995 until Schmidt's death in 2014. It is about six thousand years older than Stonehenge, and has turned the old story around: here the temple may have come before the farm. It became a World Heritage Site in 2018.
gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_history.es: Klaus Schmidt, del Instituto Arqueológico Alemán, reconoció el yacimiento en 1994 y lo excavó desde 1995 hasta su muerte en 2014. Es unos seis mil años más antiguo que Stonehenge y ha dado la vuelta a la vieja historia: aquí el templo pudo preceder a la granja. Fue declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 2018.

gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place.en: the hill of Göbekli Tepe, on a ridge above the Harran plain near Şanlıurfa
gm_arch_site_gobekli_tepe_place.es: la colina de Göbekli Tepe, en una loma sobre la llanura de Harran, cerca de Şanlıurfa

gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_dug.en: Under $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_ishtar_gate_babylon').GetName], the excavators have followed the Processional Way of Babylon to the Ishtar Gate: a double gateway of brick glazed in deep blue, with rows of yellow and white bulls and dragons in relief, its lower courses standing where the floods left them. Thousands of glazed fragments of the lions that lined the road lie in the debris.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history$
gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_ishtar_gate_babylon').GetName], los excavadores han seguido la Vía Procesional de Babilonia hasta la Puerta de Ishtar: una puerta doble de ladrillo vidriado en azul intenso, con hileras de toros y dragones amarillos y blancos en relieve, con sus hiladas inferiores en pie donde las dejaron las crecidas. Miles de fragmentos vidriados de los leones que flanqueaban el camino yacen entre los escombros.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history$

gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_found.en: Builders have quarried bricks from $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_ishtar_gate_babylon').GetName], for centuries, and the bricks are stamped with the name of Nebuchadnezzar. Our scholars are sure the city of Babylon lies beneath, and that the fragments of blue glazed brick that come out of the Kasr belong to its great gate.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history$
gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_found.es: Los constructores llevan siglos extrayendo ladrillos de $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_ishtar_gate_babylon').GetName], y los ladrillos llevan estampado el nombre de Nabucodonosor. Nuestros eruditos están seguros de que la ciudad de Babilonia yace debajo, y de que los fragmentos de ladrillo vidriado azul que salen del Kasr pertenecen a su gran puerta.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history$

gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history.en: Robert Koldewey's expedition for the German Oriental Society dug Babylon from 1899 to 1917. The glazed fragments went to Berlin under a division of finds agreed with Iraq in 1926, and the gate and part of the Processional Way were rebuilt in the Pergamon Museum, first shown in 1930. The gate's unglazed lower courses still stand in Babylon.
gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_history.es: La expedición de Robert Koldewey para la Sociedad Oriental Alemana excavó Babilonia de 1899 a 1917. Los fragmentos vidriados fueron a Berlín en virtud de un reparto de hallazgos acordado con Irak en 1926, y la puerta y parte de la Vía Procesional se reconstruyeron en el Museo de Pérgamo, expuestas por primera vez en 1930. Las hiladas inferiores sin vidriar de la puerta siguen en pie en Babilonia.

gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place.en: the mounds of Babil and Kasr by the Euphrates, near Hillah
gm_arch_site_ishtar_gate_babylon_place.es: los montículos de Babil y Kasr junto al Éufrates, cerca de Hilla

gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_dug.en: The surveyors have mapped $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_lascaux_caves').GetName]: chamber after chamber painted some seventeen thousand years ago with about six hundred animals, aurochs five metres long, horses, stags, ibex, and a wounded bison facing a man with a bird's head, and some fifteen hundred engravings, with the painters' lamps, pigments and flint tools still on the floor.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history$
gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_dug.es: Los topógrafos han cartografiado $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_lascaux_caves').GetName]: sala tras sala pintada hace unos diecisiete mil años con unos seiscientos animales, uros de cinco metros de largo, caballos, ciervos, íbices y un bisonte herido frente a un hombre con cabeza de pájaro, y unos mil quinientos grabados, con las lámparas, los pigmentos y las herramientas de sílex de los pintores aún en el suelo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history$

gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_found.en: Four teenagers from Montignac, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_lascaux_caves').GetName], following their dog into a hole left by a fallen tree, have slid down into $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place$. They went back with a lamp, and say the walls are covered with painted animals.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history$
gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_found.es: Cuatro adolescentes de Montignac, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_lascaux_caves').GetName], siguiendo a su perro hasta un agujero dejado por un árbol caído, se han deslizado hasta $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place$. Volvieron con una lámpara y dicen que las paredes están cubiertas de animales pintados.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history$

gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history.en: Marcel Ravidat and three friends found the cave in September 1940, and the Abbé Henri Breuil studied it. Opened to the public in 1948, it drew so many visitors that their breath brought algae and mould, and it was closed in 1963. Visitors now see copies: Lascaux II, opened in 1983, and Lascaux IV in 2016.
gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_history.es: Marcel Ravidat y tres amigos encontraron la cueva en septiembre de 1940, y el abate Henri Breuil la estudió. Abierta al público en 1948, atrajo a tantos visitantes que su aliento trajo algas y moho, y se cerró en 1963. Hoy los visitantes ven copias: Lascaux II, inaugurada en 1983, y Lascaux IV en 2016.

gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place.en: a cave in the hillside above Montignac, in the valley of the Vézère
gm_arch_site_lascaux_caves_place.es: una cueva en la ladera sobre Montignac, en el valle del Vézère

gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_dug.en: On $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_machu_picchu').GetName], the expedition has cut away the forest and laid bare a city of granite: temples, palaces and houses of fitted stone, terraces stepping down the mountain, fountains, and the Intihuatana, a carved stone for the sun. In its burial caves and middens lie pottery, bronze tools, ornaments and the bones of the people who lived there.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history$
gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_machu_picchu').GetName], la expedición ha talado el bosque y ha dejado al descubierto una ciudad de granito: templos, palacios y casas de piedra ajustada, terrazas que descienden por la montaña, fuentes y el Intihuatana, una piedra tallada para el sol. En sus cuevas funerarias y basureros yacen cerámica, herramientas de bronce, adornos y los huesos de las personas que vivieron allí.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history$

gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_found.en: Muleteers and farmers of the Urubamba valley speak of old stone buildings far above the river. Our scholars, searching for the last refuges of the Inca, believe $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_machu_picchu').GetName], hides a royal city the Spaniards never found.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history$
gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_found.es: Arrieros y agricultores del valle del Urubamba hablan de antiguos edificios de piedra muy por encima del río. Nuestros eruditos, que buscan los últimos refugios de los incas, creen que $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_machu_picchu').GetName], oculta una ciudad real que los españoles nunca encontraron.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history$

gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history.en: Built for the Inca emperor Pachacuti around 1450 and abandoned after the Spanish conquest, the city was known to local farmers. Hiram Bingham of Yale was guided there in 1911 by Melchor Arteaga and made it famous. Yale shipped thousands of artefacts to New Haven and returned them to Peru only in 2011 and 2012, after a long dispute.
gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_history.es: Construida para el emperador inca Pachacútec hacia 1450 y abandonada tras la conquista española, la ciudad era conocida por los agricultores de la zona. Hiram Bingham, de Yale, fue guiado hasta allí en 1911 por Melchor Arteaga y la hizo famosa. Yale envió miles de objetos a New Haven y solo los devolvió a Perú en 2011 y 2012, tras una larga disputa.

gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place.en: a ridge high above the Urubamba gorge, beneath the peak of Huayna Picchu
gm_arch_site_machu_picchu_place.es: una cresta en lo alto de la garganta del Urubamba, bajo el pico del Huayna Picchu

gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_dug.en: Under $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mawangdui_tombs').GetName], the excavators have opened three Han tombs of the family of Li Cang, Marquis of Dai, sealed in charcoal and clay in the second century BC. In nested lacquer coffins lay the marquis's wife, Xin Zhui, the body so well kept that the joints still bend, with a painted silk banner of heaven, earth and the underworld, robes of gauze, lacquerware, food, and a library written on silk: the Laozi, the Book of Changes, medical recipes and maps.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history$
gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mawangdui_tombs').GetName], los excavadores han abierto tres tumbas Han de la familia de Li Cang, marqués de Dai, selladas con carbón y arcilla en el siglo II a. C. En ataúdes de laca encajados yacía la esposa del marqués, Xin Zhui, con el cuerpo tan bien conservado que las articulaciones aún se doblan, junto a un estandarte de seda pintado con el cielo, la tierra y el inframundo, túnicas de gasa, objetos de laca, alimentos y una biblioteca escrita en seda: el Laozi, el Libro de las mutaciones, recetas médicas y mapas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history$

gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_found.en: Workers digging air-raid shelters for a military hospital in $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mawangdui_tombs').GetName], have hit a pocket of gas that burned blue when it was lit, and beneath it white clay and charcoal sealing a tomb.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history$
gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_found.es: Unos obreros que cavaban refugios antiaéreos para un hospital militar en $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mawangdui_tombs').GetName], han dado con una bolsa de gas que ardió azul al encenderse y, debajo, arcilla blanca y carbón que sellaban una tumba.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history$

gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history.en: The tombs were opened from 1972 to 1974. The autopsy of Xin Zhui found type A blood in the veins and melon seeds in the stomach; Xin Zhui died about 163 BC. The silk manuscripts include the oldest known copies of several classics and some of the oldest maps found in China. The finds are in the Hunan Museum.
gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_history.es: Las tumbas se abrieron de 1972 a 1974. La autopsia de Xin Zhui halló sangre de tipo A en las venas y semillas de melón en el estómago; Xin Zhui murió hacia 163 a. C. Los manuscritos de seda incluyen las copias más antiguas conocidas de varios clásicos y algunos de los mapas más antiguos hallados en China. Los hallazgos se conservan en el Museo de Hunan.

gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place.en: two low hills at Mawangdui, on the eastern edge of Changsha
gm_arch_site_mawangdui_tombs_place.es: dos colinas bajas en Mawangdui, en el extremo oriental de Changsha

gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_dug.en: Around and beneath $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mohenjo_daro').GetName], the excavators have uncovered a city laid out on a grid about 2500 BC: streets with covered drains, houses of baked brick with wells and bathrooms, a granary, and a great bath on the citadel. They have found carved seals by the hundred, a bronze statuette of a dancing girl, and a bearded figure in steatite they call the Priest-King.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history$
gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_dug.es: Alrededor y debajo de $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mohenjo_daro').GetName], los excavadores han sacado a la luz una ciudad trazada en cuadrícula hacia 2500 a. C.: calles con desagües cubiertos, casas de ladrillo cocido con pozos y baños, un granero y un gran baño en la ciudadela. Han hallado sellos tallados por centenares, una estatuilla de bronce de una bailarina y una figura barbada de esteatita a la que llaman el Rey-Sacerdote.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history$

gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_found.en: Brick robbers working $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mohenjo_daro').GetName], have brought out baked bricks and small square seals carved with animals and with a script nobody can read. The surveyors took the site for a Buddhist monastery a few centuries old; the seals look far older.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history$
gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_found.es: Unos saqueadores de ladrillos que trabajan en $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mohenjo_daro').GetName], han sacado ladrillos cocidos y pequeños sellos cuadrados tallados con animales y con una escritura que nadie sabe leer. Los topógrafos tomaron el lugar por un monasterio budista de unos pocos siglos de antigüedad; los sellos parecen mucho más antiguos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history$

gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history.en: R. D. Banerji of the Archaeological Survey of India dug the mound in 1922, while Daya Ram Sahni dug Harappa, and in 1924 John Marshall announced a civilization older than any then known in India. Its script is still undeciphered. The Priest-King is in Karachi and the Dancing Girl in New Delhi, divided between Pakistan and India after 1947.
gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_history.es: R. D. Banerji, del Servicio Arqueológico de la India, excavó el montículo en 1922, mientras Daya Ram Sahni excavaba Harappa, y en 1924 John Marshall anunció una civilización más antigua que cualquier otra conocida entonces en la India. Su escritura sigue sin descifrar. El Rey-Sacerdote está en Karachi y la Bailarina en Nueva Delhi, repartidos entre Pakistán y la India tras 1947.

gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place.en: a mound by the Indus near Larkana, crowned by a ruined Buddhist stupa
gm_arch_site_mohenjo_daro_place.es: un montículo junto al Indo, cerca de Larkana, coronado por una estupa budista en ruinas

gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_dug.en: Inside the walls of $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mycenae_grave_circle').GetName], just beyond the Lion Gate and beneath a ring of upright slabs, the excavators have opened five deep shaft graves holding nineteen bodies and a great weight of gold: masks beaten from sheet gold, cups, bronze daggers inlaid with hunting scenes, diadems, and hundreds of gold discs once sewn on burial clothes. The finest mask, bearded and calm, the diggers call the Mask of Agamemnon.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_history$
gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_dug.es: Dentro de las murallas que cercan $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mycenae_grave_circle').GetName], justo pasada la Puerta de los Leones y bajo un anillo de losas verticales, los excavadores han abierto cinco tumbas de fosa profundas con diecinueve cuerpos y una enorme cantidad de oro: máscaras de oro batido, copas, dagas de bronce con incrustaciones de escenas de caza, diademas y cientos de discos de oro cosidos en su día a las ropas funerarias. La máscara más fina, barbada y serena, es la que los excavadores llaman la Máscara de Agamenón.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_history$

gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_found.en: Pausanias wrote that Agamemnon and the companions murdered with the king lay buried inside the walls of Mycenae. Our scholars trust Pausanias and point to $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mycenae_grave_circle').GetName], where the Lion Gate still stands half buried in its own rubble.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_history$
gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_found.es: Pausanias escribió que Agamenón y los compañeros asesinados con el rey yacían enterrados dentro de las murallas de Micenas. Nuestros eruditos confían en Pausanias y señalan $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_mycenae_grave_circle').GetName], donde la Puerta de los Leones sigue en pie medio enterrada en sus propios escombros.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_history$

gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_histor.en: Heinrich Schliemann dug Grave Circle A in 1876 and is said to have claimed to have gazed on the face of Agamemnon. The graves are in fact some three centuries older than any Trojan War, from about 1550 BC. The finds are in the National Archaeological Museum in Athens. A second circle, Grave Circle B, was found outside the walls in 1951.
gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_histor.es: Heinrich Schliemann excavó el Círculo de Tumbas A en 1876 y se dice que afirmó haber contemplado el rostro de Agamenón. En realidad, las tumbas son unos tres siglos anteriores a cualquier guerra de Troya, de hacia 1550 a. C. Los hallazgos están en el Museo Arqueológico Nacional de Atenas. Un segundo círculo, el Círculo de Tumbas B, se encontró fuera de las murallas en 1951.

gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place.en: the citadel of Mycenae, in the hills above the plain of Argos
gm_arch_site_mycenae_grave_circle_place.es: la ciudadela de Micenas, en las colinas sobre la llanura de Argos

gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_dug.en: From the farmers who dug at $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nag_hammadi_library').GetName], and the dealers they sold to, our scholars have gathered thirteen leather-bound papyrus books of the fourth century holding some fifty texts in Coptic: Gnostic gospels, among them the Gospel of Thomas and the Gospel of Philip, apocalypses and treatises, and a piece of Plato's Republic, books the early Church had condemned and someone buried to save.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history$
gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_dug.es: De los agricultores que excavaron en $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nag_hammadi_library').GetName], y de los comerciantes a quienes vendieron, nuestros eruditos han reunido trece libros de papiro encuadernados en cuero, del siglo IV, con unos cincuenta textos en copto: evangelios gnósticos, entre ellos el Evangelio de Tomás y el Evangelio de Felipe, apocalipsis y tratados, y un fragmento de la República de Platón, libros que la Iglesia primitiva había condenado y que alguien enterró para salvarlos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history$

gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_found.en: Farmers digging for nitrate fertiliser at $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nag_hammadi_library').GetName], have unearthed a sealed red clay jar. Fearing a jinn and hoping for gold, they broke it open and found old books bound in leather; some have already been sold, and pages of one were burned in a kitchen oven.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history$
gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_found.es: Unos agricultores que cavaban en busca de fertilizante de nitrato en $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nag_hammadi_library').GetName], han desenterrado una jarra de arcilla roja sellada. Temiendo a un yinn y esperando oro, la rompieron y encontraron libros antiguos encuadernados en cuero; algunos ya se han vendido, y las páginas de uno se quemaron en un horno de cocina.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history$

gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history.en: Muhammad Ali al-Samman and brothers found the jar in December 1945. The books passed through dealers, and one reached the Jung Institute in Zurich, before nearly all were gathered in the Coptic Museum in Cairo. A facsimile edition published from 1972 to 1977 made the texts available, and they changed the study of early Christianity.
gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_history.es: Muhammad Ali al-Samman y sus hermanos encontraron la jarra en diciembre de 1945. Los libros pasaron por manos de comerciantes, y uno llegó al Instituto Jung de Zúrich, antes de que casi todos se reunieran en el Museo Copto de El Cairo. Una edición facsímil publicada de 1972 a 1977 puso los textos al alcance de todos, y cambiaron el estudio del cristianismo primitivo.

gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place.en: the foot of the Jabal al-Tarif cliffs near Nag Hammadi
gm_arch_site_nag_hammadi_library_place.es: la base de los acantilados de Yabal al-Tarif, cerca de Nag Hammadi

gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_dug.en: The excavators have tunnelled into $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nineveh_library').GetName], and found the palaces of Sennacherib and Ashurbanipal: room after room of carved reliefs of sieges, lion hunts and deportations, gateways guarded by winged bulls, and in the archive rooms tens of thousands of clay tablets in cuneiform, the library of Ashurbanipal, with the Epic of Gilgamesh among them.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history$
gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_dug.es: Los excavadores han abierto túneles en $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nineveh_library').GetName], y han hallado los palacios de Senaquerib y Asurbanipal: sala tras sala de relieves tallados de asedios, cacerías de leones y deportaciones, puertas custodiadas por toros alados, y en las salas de archivo decenas de miles de tablillas de arcilla en cuneiforme, la biblioteca de Asurbanipal, con la Epopeya de Gilgamesh entre ellas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history$

gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_found.en: Our scholars have read the Bible and the classical historians against the map, and they place Nineveh, the capital of the Assyrian kings, under $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nineveh_library').GetName]. The villagers who dig there for building stone turn up carved slabs, and beneath them, the scholars believe, lie palaces.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history$
gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_found.es: Nuestros eruditos han leído la Biblia y a los historiadores clásicos con el mapa en la mano, y sitúan Nínive, la capital de los reyes asirios, bajo $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_nineveh_library').GetName]. Los aldeanos que cavan allí en busca de piedra de construcción sacan lajas talladas, y debajo, creen los eruditos, yacen palacios.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history$

gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history.en: Paul-Émile Botta, the French consul at Mosul, dug at Kuyunjik in 1842 before moving to Khorsabad. Austen Henry Layard tunnelled into Sennacherib's palace from 1847, and Hormuzd Rassam found Ashurbanipal's North Palace in 1853. The reliefs and tablets went to the British Museum, where in 1872 George Smith read the story of a great flood on one of them.
gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_history.es: Paul-Émile Botta, cónsul francés en Mosul, excavó en Kuyunjik en 1842 antes de trasladarse a Jorsabad. Austen Henry Layard abrió túneles en el palacio de Senaquerib desde 1847, y Hormuzd Rassam encontró el Palacio Norte de Asurbanipal en 1853. Los relieves y las tablillas fueron al Museo Británico, donde en 1872 George Smith leyó en una de ellas la historia de un gran diluvio.

gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place.en: the mounds of Kuyunjik and Nebi Yunus on the east bank of the Tigris
gm_arch_site_nineveh_library_place.es: los montículos de Kuyunjik y Nebi Yunus, en la orilla oriental del Tigris

gm_arch_site_olympia_dug.en: Out of the silt of $gm_arch_site_olympia_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_olympia').GetName], the excavators have uncovered the sanctuary of Zeus: the foundations of the god's temple and the sculptures of its pediments, the Temple of Hera, the treasuries of the Greek cities, the tunnel to the stadium and the workshop of Pheidias, and in the ruins of the Temple of Hera the marble Hermes carrying the infant Dionysus that Pausanias said was by Praxiteles.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_olympia_history$
gm_arch_site_olympia_dug.es: Del limo que cubría $gm_arch_site_olympia_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_olympia').GetName], los excavadores han sacado a la luz el santuario de Zeus: los cimientos del templo del dios y las esculturas de sus frontones, el templo de Hera, los tesoros de las ciudades griegas, el túnel hacia el estadio y el taller de Fidias, y en las ruinas del templo de Hera el Hermes de mármol con el niño Dioniso en brazos que Pausanias dijo que era obra de Praxíteles.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_olympia_history$

gm_arch_site_olympia_found.en: Pausanias described the sanctuary of Zeus at Olympia, where the Games were held for a thousand years, statue by statue. Floods and landslides have buried it under metres of silt, but our scholars place it in $gm_arch_site_olympia_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_olympia').GetName], and French surveyors have already found the floor of its temple.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_olympia_history$
gm_arch_site_olympia_found.es: Pausanias describió estatua por estatua el santuario de Zeus en Olimpia, donde se celebraron los Juegos durante mil años. Las crecidas y los corrimientos de tierra lo han enterrado bajo metros de limo, pero nuestros eruditos lo sitúan en $gm_arch_site_olympia_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_olympia').GetName], y los topógrafos franceses ya han hallado el suelo de su templo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_olympia_history$

gm_arch_site_olympia_history.en: The French Expédition scientifique de Morée found the Temple of Zeus in 1829. The German excavation under Ernst Curtius from 1875 to 1881 was the first to agree with Greece that every find would stay in the country, a model for many after it; the Hermes was found in 1877. The Olympic flame is lit at the Temple of Hera for every modern Games.
gm_arch_site_olympia_history.es: La francesa Expédition scientifique de Morée encontró el templo de Zeus en 1829. La excavación alemana dirigida por Ernst Curtius de 1875 a 1881 fue la primera en acordar con Grecia que todo hallazgo se quedaría en el país, modelo para muchas posteriores; el Hermes apareció en 1877. La llama olímpica se enciende en el templo de Hera para cada edición de los Juegos modernos.

gm_arch_site_olympia_place.en: the valley of the Alpheios below the hill of Kronos
gm_arch_site_olympia_place.es: el valle del Alfeo, bajo la colina de Cronos

gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_dug.en: Under the turf and blue clay of $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_oseberg_ship').GetName], the excavators have laid bare a Viking ship of oak twenty-one metres long, its prow and stern carved with interlaced beasts, buried with two women, a burial chamber, a cart, sledges, beds, tapestries and the bones of horses and dogs. Grave robbers took the jewellery long ago; the wood they left is the finest carving of the Viking age.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history$
gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_dug.es: Bajo el césped y la arcilla azul que cubren $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_oseberg_ship').GetName], los excavadores han dejado al descubierto un barco vikingo de roble de veintiún metros de eslora, con la proa y la popa talladas con bestias entrelazadas, enterrado con dos mujeres, una cámara funeraria, un carro, trineos, camas, tapices y los huesos de caballos y perros. Los saqueadores de tumbas se llevaron las joyas hace mucho; la madera que dejaron es la talla más fina de la era vikinga.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history$

gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_found.en: A farmer digging into $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_oseberg_ship').GetName], has struck carved timbers. The blue clay and turf have kept them sound, and the antiquaries of the university say they belong to a ship.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history$
gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_found.es: Un agricultor que cavaba en $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_oseberg_ship').GetName], ha topado con maderos tallados. La arcilla azul y el césped los han mantenido en buen estado, y los anticuarios de la universidad dicen que pertenecen a un barco.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history$

gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history.en: Knut Rom, who farmed Oseberg, found the ship in 1903, and Gabriel Gustafson of the University of Kristiania dug it in 1904. Tree rings date the burial to 834. The ship, cart and sledges took two decades to restore and are shown at Bygdøy in Oslo.
gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_history.es: Knut Rom, que cultivaba Oseberg, encontró el barco en 1903, y Gabriel Gustafson, de la Universidad de Kristiania, lo excavó en 1904. Los anillos de los árboles datan el enterramiento en 834. El barco, el carro y los trineos tardaron dos décadas en restaurarse y se exhiben en Bygdøy, en Oslo.

gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place.en: the great burial mound on the Oseberg farm near Tønsberg
gm_arch_site_oseberg_ship_place.es: el gran túmulo funerario de la granja de Oseberg, cerca de Tønsberg

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_dug.en: From $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, on the edge of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName], the recovery team has freed a man who died about 3300 BC, mummified by the cold, with clothes of hide and grass, a bearskin cap, a copper axe hafted in yew, an unfinished longbow, a quiver of arrows, a flint dagger, birch-bark cases for embers and a kit of medicinal fungi. An arrowhead lodged in the left shoulder shows how the Iceman died.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_dug.es: Desde $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, en el límite de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName], el equipo de recuperación ha liberado a un hombre que murió hacia 3300 a. C., momificado por el frío, con ropas de piel y hierba, un gorro de piel de oso, un hacha de cobre enmangada en tejo, un arco largo sin terminar, un carcaj con flechas, una daga de sílex, estuches de corteza de abedul para brasas y un botiquín de hongos medicinales. Una punta de flecha alojada en el hombro izquierdo muestra cómo murió el Hombre de Hielo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_found.en: Two hikers coming down from the Finail peak have found a body melting out of the ice in $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, on the edge of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName]. The police took it for a lost climber, but the axe beside it has a copper blade.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_found.es: Dos excursionistas que bajaban del pico Finail han encontrado un cuerpo que va quedando libre del hielo al derretirse en $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, en el límite de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName]. La policía lo tomó por un alpinista perdido, pero el hacha que tiene al lado lleva una hoja de cobre.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history.en: Erika and Helmut Simon found the body on 19 September 1991, a few metres inside Italy; the first, careless recovery broke its hip with a pneumatic drill. Austria and Italy settled where the body lay, and since 1998 the Iceman has lain in a cold cell in the South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology in Bolzano. The arrowhead was found in 2001; the body carries sixty-one tattoos.
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history.es: Erika y Helmut Simon encontraron el cuerpo el 19 de septiembre de 1991, a pocos metros dentro de Italia; la primera recuperación, descuidada, le rompió la cadera con un martillo neumático. Austria e Italia determinaron en qué país yacía el cuerpo, y desde 1998 el Hombre de Hielo reposa en una celda fría del Museo Arqueológico de Tirol del Sur, en Bolzano. La punta de flecha se halló en 2001; el cuerpo lleva sesenta y un tatuajes.

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place.en: a hollow in the rock at the Tisenjoch pass, high in the Ötztal Alps
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place.es: una hondonada en la roca del paso de Tisenjoch, en lo alto de los Alpes de Ötztal

gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_dug.en: On $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_palace_of_knossos').GetName], the excavators have uncovered a palace of some thirteen hundred rooms around a great court: storerooms of jars as tall as a man, light wells, staircases, a stone throne, drains and bathrooms, and walls painted with bull-leapers, lilies and dolphins.
